microtopics.title: Rotational Dynamics & Angular Momentum Conservation
entry_assumptions: **Angular Momentum Origin Precondition**: Angular momentum $\vec{L} = \vec{r} \times \vec{p}$ and torque $\vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F}$ **must always be defined with respect to the same specified origin point**. Shifting the origin changes both torque and angular momentum.

**Rolling Without Slipping Condition**: Pure rolling on a stationary surface requires the contact point instantaneous velocity to be zero: $v_{\text{cm}} = \omega R$. Static friction performs zero net work during pure rolling.
microtopics.inferential_jump: Moment of inertia as rotational inertia: $I = \int r^2 dm$; parallel axis theorem $I = I_{\text{cm}} + M d^2$; perpendicular axis theorem $I_z = I_x + I_y$ for laminar bodies.

teaching_path.action: Conservation of angular momentum: $\sum \vec{\tau}_{\text{ext}} = 0 \implies \vec{L}_{\text{total}} = \text{const} \implies I_1 \omega_1 = I_2 \omega_2$.

Total kinetic energy of rolling body: $K_{\text{total}} = K_{\text{trans}} + K_{\text{rot}} = \frac{1}{2}M v_{\text{cm}}^2 + \frac{1}{2}I_{\text{cm}}\omega^2 = \frac{1}{2}M v_{\text{cm}}^2\left(1 + \frac{k^2}{R^2}\right)$.
Analyzing acceleration down an incline: $a_{\text{cm}} = \frac{g\sin\theta}{1 + I_{\text{cm}}/(MR^2)}$.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Assuming friction always points backward on a rolling cylinder or bicycle wheel.
misconceptions.repair: Static friction opposes relative slippage between surfaces. On the rear driven wheel of a bicycle, friction points *forward*, propelling the bike forward.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Applying $L_i = L_f$ about an origin where an external normal force exerts non-zero torque.
misconceptions.repair: Angular momentum is conserved only about an axis or point where the net external torque is zero ($\tau_{\text{ext}} = 0$).
